measurement: oracle-mutation audit wall-clock on a REAL battery deliverable, and the per-criterion attribution it now yields (#1195 item 3, L4-KILLS)

hardware.gpu: Intel Arc 140V (Xe2) - NOT used; this stage is CPU-only subprocess work

toolchain.oracle_runner: uv run --no-project --with pytest==9.1.1 --with hypothesis==6.155.7 python -m pytest -q <oracle>
toolchain.note: The runner was NOT substituted. A sibling test on this module injects `sys.executable -m pytest` (0.9 s/invocation); the pinned command costs ~5.67 s because uv builds a fresh ephemeral environment per run and the audit's per-run isolated home defeats caching.

methodology: The banked run dir was COPIED to scratch and the operator's evidence left untouched; the delivered tree is copied internally by the stage. Each configuration ran once (n=1) through the real entry point tools.dispatch_harness.green_quality.mutation.audit_green_oracles. Other agents were active on the CPU during both runs.

results.finding: One planned mutant was silently dropped. The status still reads `run` (a complete audit), not `partial-budget`, because the loop's budget checks pass on a positive-but-tiny remaining and the squeezed mutant becomes an uncounted machinery miss. The denominator shrinks; the score does not.

results.config: per_job_budget_s = 1800.0 (generous, to isolate the budget effect)
results.finding: Reproduces the operator's original 2026-07-30 banked figure (17/20) exactly, which also confirms the attribution change does not alter mutation outcomes.

cost_reading.estimate_basis: 20 x 5.67 s, from a two-function fixture
cost_reading.consequence: The measured cost of ONE real GREEN exceeds the per-job budget (350.5 > 300) and a four-GREEN night would need ~1402 s against a 900 s stage cap, so later GREENs would be stamped skipped-battery-budget and reach no L4 rung.

before.fingerprint: oracle_coverage=3/6 L3+ (weak:0 gap:0 undecidable:3; L4 not measured)

after.fingerprint: oracle_coverage=3/6 L3+ (weak:0 gap:0 undecidable:3; L4 killed:3 survived:0 unmeasured:3)

attribution_yield.note: The headline L3+ figure is unchanged by design: L3 and L4 are both covered, so attribution refines strength without moving the covered count. The 3 unmeasured are the 3 UNDECIDABLE criteria, which never reached L3 and so can support no rung.

attribution_findings: The whole-file 17/20 hid that one of the three survivors (early_return, app/word_frequencies.py:27) sits in `word_frequencies_from_text` - a function no test imports. It is not a weakness in the `word_frequencies` exam at all.

The other two survivors (boundary + constant, app/neighbor_pairs.py:33) sit in `neighbor_pairs`, which SIMULTANEOUSLY earned L4 via its own test. A criterion can hold the rung and a blind spot at once, so surviving loci are now reported per criterion regardless of level.

seam_test.what_it_proves: REAL pinned uv runner -> REAL audit -> banked sidecar -> REAL traceability.assess_run -> L4-KILLS, with nothing substituted.

not_measured: Run-to-run variance: n=1 per configuration, and both runs shared the CPU with other agents. The 19-vs-20 delta is attributed to the budget squeeze because the generous-budget re-run recovered the 20th mutant, but the squeeze was not isolated by instrumenting the per-mutant timeout directly.
Cost on deliverables larger than this four-module tree, or with more than the _MAX_TARGET_FILES=10 import targets.
Whether the 5.67 s per-invocation figure still holds under the concurrent load these runs saw; only the end-to-end 350.5 s was timed.
Node/web exams: no host .js mutation runner exists (#830), so attribution is python-only.

Attribution behaviour on an exam whose repo pytest config suppresses the failure summary. The suppression itself WAS measured directly (addopts = -rN --tb=no removes both the short summary and the traceback), and the parser is locked against it, but no real battery deliverable carrying such a config was audited.
